summary: Both round-1 majors are genuinely closed, and I verified it by re-running the mutants myself rather than taking the report's word for it. Baseline: 84/84 Playwright + 84/84 vitest green on the unmodified tree (Node 22 via /snap/bin). Mutant A (GroupHeader renders the raw stored title) now fails exactly one test — 3.4 — and mutant B (GroupSettingsPopup heading renders the raw stored title) fails exactly one test — 8.1, with the diagnostic 'Expected substring: In Progress / Received string: Settings: '. Neither mutant leaked failures into any other scenario, so the two new assertions are precise, not blast-radius noise. Placing them inside existing scenarios instead of adding new ones was the right call and costs nothing: neither selector appeared anywhere under tests/ before this commit, so both assertions are pure new coverage with zero duplication, and each earns its place by killing a mutant no other test kills. The 3.4 refactor (locating .tm-group-header once, then scoping the counter through it) is semantically identical to the old direct selector and weakens nothing — Playwright strict mode confirms exactly one header matches. What remains open is what was already open in round 1 and is not the executor's to fix. Mutant C (inverted EmptyState ternary) still leaves the whole suite at 84/84 — it is now the only one of the four rewritten display sites with no regression signal at all. And I sharpened finding 6 with new evidence: mutant D (CollapsibleGroup renders the raw stored title) kills 4 core.spec.ts tests, but every one of them fails as a locator.click timeout at helpers.ts:104 waiting for filter({ hasText: 'Backlog' }) — not one is an assertion about the title. The collapsible title's entire regression signal is the text-matching locator Task 09 exists to delete. The deferrals in items 2, 3 and 6 are acceptable as decisions, but two of them currently point at a decisions-log entry for Task 06 that does not exist yet, and the wording planned for it is already stale: one mutant survives now, not three.

findings.issue: Round 1 finding 6, now with harder evidence and a narrower window. The fix closed two of the three name-display sites with class-based assertions that will survive Task 09's locator migration; the third, '.tm-collapsible-group__title', still has zero assertion in any file under tests/ — grep confirms the selector appears only in the compiled harness bundle. Its regression signal is entirely incidental: I re-ran the collapsible mutant (title = storedTitle instead of the resolved name) and it fails 4 core.spec.ts tests (3.2, 6.3, 6.4, 7.1), but all four fail identically as 'locator.click: Test timeout exceeded / waiting for locator(.tm-collapsible-group__header).filter({ hasText: Backlog })' at helpers.ts:104. Not one failure is an assertion about what the header renders — the tests die because they cannot find a button to click. Task 09 is chartered to replace exactly that hasText filter with an identifier-based locator (its own file lists 'grep -rn hasText: Backlog|Focus|... tests/e2e/' as a verification step). The moment it lands, this site's coverage drops from four incidental failures to zero, and nothing in Task 09's file warns about it.
findings.recommendation: One line, symmetric with the two that just worked, inside existing test 7.1 — no new scenario, so Task 09's 'core.spec.ts — 35 scenarios' precondition still holds. In 7.1 (core.spec.ts:245), immediately after 'await expandGroup(page, "backlog")' and the existing toBeVisible check, the body is in the DOM so the group container resolves by identifier: await expect(page.locator('.tm-collapsible-group:has([data-group-id="backlog"]) .tm-collapsible-group__title')).toHaveText('Backlog'). That is the 3.4 pattern verbatim. Verify by re-running mutant D: the failure must move from a locator.click timeout at helpers.ts:104 to a toHaveText failure inside 7.1. If the orchestrator prefers to keep this in Task 09, then Task 09's file must carry it as a blocking precondition — land the assertion first, migrate the locators second, and re-run mutant D afterwards to prove the identifier-based replacement still goes red. Doing it here is cheaper and removes the ordering constraint entirely.

findings.issue: Re-verified unchanged: I inverted the ternary (trim() !== '' -> trim() === '') and the full suite stayed at 84/84 green. This is now the only one of the four display sites this task rewrote that no test at any level can see, and it is also the only NEW decision logic the task introduced — Task 05's unit tests cover resolveGroupTitle, not this branch. The deferral itself is correct and I said so in round 1: the task text mandates the placement inside EmptyState and forbids a second export in groupTitle.ts, so the executor cannot close this without a spec amendment. But the deferral does not make the gap smaller — it runs from wave 3 to Task 10 in wave 7, and the acceptance criterion it backs ('name and hint can never disagree, because both use the same emptiness rule') is enforced by nothing and, per Task 10's own note that a whitespace-only title is unreachable through the UI, cannot be enforced by E2E either.
findings.recommendation: Orchestrator decision, unchanged from round 1, and it is now the single open item with no compensating coverage. Either (a) make Task 10's Sc.13 blocking and accept the four-wave window explicitly — which covers the reachable case ('' and a real name) but never the shared-emptiness-rule criterion; or (b) amend the spec to extract src/ui/emptyStateKey.ts exporting emptyStateKey(groupId: GroupId, storedTitle: string): TranslationKey, leaving Task 05's one-export constraint on groupTitle.ts untouched and reducing EmptyState to a one-line call. Unit test in tests/unit/emptyStateKey.test.ts: '' -> 'emptyState.focus'; '   ' and '\t' -> 'emptyState.focus'; 'Долгострой' -> 'emptyState.renamed'; each of the six GroupIds -> its own template key; plus a table-driven consistency assertion pairing it with resolveGroupTitle over shared inputs, so the two emptiness rules cannot drift. Only (b) makes the 'can never disagree' criterion testable.

findings.location: docs/features/0011-feat-group-customization/0011-feat-group-customization-task-06.md — Section: Context Files (tests/e2e/core.spec.ts entry) and Section: TDD Anchor
findings.issue: Downgraded from major, because the fix inverted which paragraph is wrong and the dangerous direction is gone. The TDD Anchor's conclusion is now true — core.spec.ts really does exercise the normal header title and the popup heading — even though its stated reason (asserting '.tm-group-header__counter' constrains the title) was never valid. Meanwhile the Context Files paragraph, which was the accurate one in round 1, is now factually false: 'A broken fallback in the ordinary group header or in the group settings popup would leave this suite green' is empirically disproven by mutants A and B, which I ran against this exact tree. The two paragraphs still contradict each other; the document still misdescribes its own suite. The harm is smaller now — a reader who believes the stale sentence understates coverage rather than overstating it, which produces redundancy rather than false confidence — but Task 10 reads this file to decide what its scenarios must cover, and it will now be told the popup heading is unguarded when 8.1 guards it.
findings.recommendation: One sentence, if the orchestrator is willing to touch the task file at all: in the Context Files entry for core.spec.ts, replace 'A broken fallback in the ordinary group header or in the group settings popup would leave this suite green' with 'Since review round 1 the suite asserts the default name in the ordinary header (3.4) and in the popup heading (8.1); the collapsed header is still matched only by its visible text, and the empty-state hint key is unguarded.' If the file is frozen, the same sentence must appear in the decisions log entry, because that is where Task 10 will look next.

findings.issue: Items 2 and 5 of the fix report are discharged by writing to the decisions log, and the log currently has no Task 06 entry at all (grep for 'Task 06' returns one incidental mention inside the Task 02 entry). I cannot verify a deferral whose artifact does not exist, and the mutation evidence this review produced lives nowhere else — the throwaway spec was correctly deleted, so prose in a log is the only surviving form. The planned wording is also already stale: the report says it will record 'your three surviving mutants', but after this commit only one of them survives. Mutant A dies in 3.4, mutant B dies in 8.1; the survivor is the EmptyState ternary. Recording three would hand Task 10 a false map of the gap and could send it to write two redundant default-path scenarios that duplicate 3.4 and 8.1.
findings.recommendation: In the Task 06 entry, record the mutation results as they stand after b272b83, not as they stood after 8dfff69: (1) GroupHeader raw title -> kills core.spec.ts 3.4 only; (2) GroupSettingsPopup raw heading -> kills 8.1 only; (3) CollapsibleGroup raw title -> kills 3.2/6.3/6.4/7.1, but all four as locator.click timeouts at helpers.ts:104, so this is locator-incidental coverage that Task 09 removes; (4) EmptyState inverted ternary -> the whole suite stays 84/84, the one genuinely surviving mutant. Then add the item-5 recipe as agreed: seeding titles via a versioned snapshot through window.__test.resetData (routes through migrateData, tests/harness/main.ts:80-95); truncation observable as scrollWidth > clientWidth on the title at a 300px viewport with a 38-char name; sibling controls keeping their 24px box, which is what proves flex-shrink:0 rather than the truncation alone. Also record the new prop name and its string-not-boolean shape, which the task's own Post-completion checklist already requires.
